summary: Duplicate function executions after HSM-backed API-key rotation during Go SDK streaming with parallel goroutines
description: Issue summary: Customer reports duplicated function/tool invocations observed in production after their HSM-backed API-key rotated mid-stream. Impact: duplicate downstream side-effects (duplicate database writes and external webhook posts) from the same logical user request. Context: DataForge Analytics runs the Go streaming SDK in a high-throughput backend where each incoming task fan-outs to 8 goroutines that each create a stream session and may trigger function calls via the "function_call" tool. They have HSM key rotation configured in their private deployment; rotation occurred while long-lived streams were active.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure private deployment with HSM-based API key rotation set to rotate keys every 15 minutes.
2) Run multiple long-lived streaming sessions from Go SDK with goroutine pool >= 8 and per-session retry/backoff enabled.
3) Trigger a sequence that causes the model to issue a function_call (tool invocation) while a rotation event occurs.
4) Observe downstream system (DB/webhook) for duplicate entries/POSTs and compare funcall IDs returned by Redwood and the client's idempotency headers.
comments: 2026-03-10T09:12 Jordan Patel (Support): Initial triage from customer indicates pairs of identical business events tied to roughly-simultaneous func_call_ids. Customer attached DB rows showing duplicated payloads with different func_call_ids but same idempotency_token.

2026-03-10T11:05 Maya Singh (SRE): Asked customer for trace IDs and exact SDK version. Potentially related to idempotency token normalization across goroutines during key refresh. Requested short-term mitigation: disable concurrent stream fan-out until we confirm behavior.
2026-03-10T14:32 DataForge Dev (customer): Provided traces (trace:rf-3312) and confirmed they are on sdk-go v1.18.2 using our private VPC. Noted that duplicates spike during rotation windows only.

2026-03-11T08:45 Riley Thompson (Eng): Reproduced locally in private-deploy sim with stubbed HSM rotation. Observed token regeneration in goroutine 3 after rotation while goroutine 0 retained previous session metadata, causing service to accept two tokens as distinct. Filed hypothesis and linked PR for SDK change.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: HSM rotation path updates signing keys and an SDK layer re-signs/normalizes idempotency tokens per goroutine. Parallel streams may compute different canonical forms for the same logical token across the rotation boundary, bypassing de-dup checks in serving-runtime.

Trace rf-3312 shows two func_call_ids fc-5501 / fc-5502 with identical function payloads and identical session_nonce but different token sign bytes; server treated both as unique because token hash comparison uses raw token string post-auth normalization.

Serving-runtime logs show duplicate_check uses normalized-token stored in memcache keyed by (customer+normalized_token). During rotation the auth layer mutated token presentation briefly, resulting in both forms being accepted.
Reproduced with sdk-go v1.18.2; switching to pinned v1.17.x avoided immediate repro (older SDK keeps pre-rotation token opaque).
Temporary mitigation confirmed: set HSM rotation window to occur during low-traffic or use soft-rotation (overlap period) > 60s to allow in-flight streams to finish.

Proposed long-term fix: (a) make serving-runtime de-dup robust to signing-key rotation by normalizing tokens to a stable canonical form independent of signing key and/or store a rotation-aware idempotency index; (b) patch sdk-go to avoid re-canonicalizing tokens mid-stream (PR referenced below).
resolution: Workaround and next steps: 1) Immediate: advised customer to enable soft-rotation with 90s overlap for HSM key rollouts and to temporarily reduce goroutine fan-out to 2 for critical long-lived streams. 2) Short-term engineering: SDK change submitted to prevent per-goroutine token re-canonicalization (see github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/1989). 3) Runtime change: issue opened to make de-dup resilient to token presentation differences across rotation (runtime task tracked under ENG-1286). 4) Postmortem: schedule joint postmortem with DataForge next week to review rollout safety. Customer confirmed workaround reduced duplicates to zero during next rotation window.
notes: This ticket intersects HSM rotation, auth normalization, and streaming idempotency — cross-team coordination required (Auth, SDK, Runtime). Keep Slack thread #support-private-hsm and link to incident INC-2026-03-09-11 for customer-facing communications.
